svg.title: Four ways to run compute
svg.desc: Four stacks compare ways to run applications. A physical server runs one operating system and its apps directly on hardware; it takes days or weeks to deploy and you buy the hardware. Virtual machines run on a hypervisor, each with its own guest operating system and app; they start in minutes, are billed while running, and include Hyper-V, VMware, Azure Virtual Machines, and Amazon EC2. Containers share the host operating system through a container runtime, each holding an app and its libraries; they start in seconds, and examples are Docker, Kubernetes, AKS, and EKS. Serverless runs only your function code when an event occurs, on infrastructure the provider fully manages; it starts in milliseconds to seconds, is billed per run and its duration, and examples are Azure Functions and AWS Lambda. Moving from physical servers to serverless, the provider manages more, workloads start faster, and billing becomes more precise.
